opening.text: Shake a snow globe and the whole scene whirls. You can't see a thing. But set it down and wait. Slowly the snow settles, and the scene comes clear again. Our minds can feel like that snow globe. Peace is what happens when we set it down and let it settle.

mainMessage.text: Peace is the stillness that comes when we set our worries down in the Savior's hands.

blocks.text: **An invitation** The Savior doesn't wait for us to be calm before we come. He invites us as we are.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Savior’s invitation to come to Him is an offer of peace.
Come as you are.
**Not as the world gives** The world offers quick fixes. The Savior gives something deeper.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
But He said that He would give peace in His way, not in the world’s way.
His peace is different.
**A quiet voice** When the snow settles, we can hear again. The Spirit speaks softly.
Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
The Spirit will speak peace to your soul.
Listen for the Spirit.
**Peace in the middle of the storm** The snow globe may still be shaken. Peace doesn't mean no trouble. It means we are held in it.
These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
But we can have His peace with us irrespective of the troubles of the world.
His peace stays.
**Learning to be still** We settle by learning of Christ and walking in His Spirit.
Learn of me, and listen to my words; walk in the meekness of my Spirit, and you shall have peace in me.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
That peace comes from the assurances spoken by a still, small voice.
Learn of Him.
**Passing it along** Once our own snow has settled, we can help someone else's settle too.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
I pray that you may find peace, help many others to find it, and pass it along.
Pass it along.

story.title: Jesus calms the sea

blocks.text: The disciples were in a boat when a storm hit. Jesus was asleep in the back.

And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
The Savior spoke to the storm, and it obeyed. He can speak to the storm in us too.

application.text: First, find a quiet five minutes today. Second, name one worry and tell Heavenly Father about it. Third, sit still, and listen.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ gives peace that the world can't give. I know Heavenly Father hears us when we ask for calm. I know the Holy Ghost speaks peace to our souls. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A ship in a harbor can still be tossed by waves. What keeps it from drifting is the anchor. The anchor doesn't stop the water from moving. It holds the ship in place anyway. That is how peace works in a rough life. It is not a calm sea. It is an anchor.

mainMessage.text: Peace is an anchor. It holds us steady even when the waters are rough.

blocks.text: **The harbor is Christ** The Savior invites us to come to Him, and that is where the anchor holds.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Savior’s invitation to come to Him is an offer of peace.
Come to the harbor.
**Not a shallow anchor** The world's peace drags in the first storm. The Savior's holds.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
But He said that He would give peace in His way, not in the world’s way.
His anchor holds.
**The line to the anchor** An anchor needs a line to the ship. The Spirit is that line to us.
Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
The Spirit will speak peace to your soul.
Stay connected.
**Waves will come** The anchor isn't for calm days. It is for the days the wind blows.
These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
But we can have His peace with us irrespective of the troubles of the world.
Hold in the wind.
**Set the anchor daily** We don't set an anchor once and forget it. We learn of Him and set it again each day.
Learn of me, and listen to my words; walk in the meekness of my Spirit, and you shall have peace in me.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
That peace comes from the assurances spoken by a still, small voice.
Set it daily.
**A harbor for others** A steady ship can be a refuge for other boats. We can help others find peace too.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
I pray that you may find peace, help many others to find it, and pass it along.
Be a harbor.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt held steady during hard days. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The soldiers of Helaman

blocks.text: Helaman's young soldiers faced a hard war. They prayed for strength.

Therefore we did pour out our souls in prayer to God, that he would strengthen us and deliver us out of the hands of our enemies, yea, and also give us strength that we might retain our cities, and our lands, and our possessions, for the support of our people. Yea, and it came to pass that the Lord our God did visit us with assurances that he would deliver us; yea, insomuch that he did speak peace to our souls, and did grant unto us great faith, and did cause us that we should hope for our deliverance in him.
The war didn't stop right away. But the Lord spoke peace to their souls. They held steady because of it.

Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.

Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.

Learn the way.
**Room for others** Once we have a quiet room, we can invite someone else in.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they found peace after a hard season. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The woman who touched His garment

blocks.text: A woman had been ill for twelve years. She had spent everything on doctors. She came to Jesus Christ in faith.

And a woman having an issue of blood twelve years, which had spent all her living upon physicians, neither could be healed of any, Came behind him, and touched the border of his garment: and immediately her issue of blood stanched. And he said unto her, Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
She reached out in her need, and He sent her away in peace. Peace begins when we reach for Him.

application.text: First, choose one small place and time you can be quiet each day. Second, pray there, even for a minute. Third, write down any feeling of peace that comes.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior opens a door of peace to every one of us. I know Heavenly Father listens in the quiet. I know the Holy Ghost brings calm to troubled hearts. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: When a storm bends a tall tree, the branches whip about. But the roots go deep, and the tree stays put. You can't see the roots. You only see the tree standing after the wind passes. Peace in a person is a lot like those roots. It is unseen, deep and steady.

mainMessage.text: Peace is a root system. It keeps us standing when the wind blows hard.

blocks.text: **Where the roots go** The roots reach toward the Savior. He is the source of water.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Savior’s invitation to come to Him is an offer of peace.
Reach toward Him.
**Deeper than the world's soil** Shallow soil doesn't hold a tree. The Savior's peace goes deeper than the world's.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
But He said that He would give peace in His way, not in the world’s way.
Go deeper.
**Water from below** The roots drink water we can't see. The Spirit speaks peace in ways we feel more than see.
Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.
The Spirit will speak peace to your soul.
Drink from below.
**Standing in the wind** The wind doesn't ask permission. Roots keep the tree standing.
These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
But we can have His peace with us irrespective of the troubles of the world.
Stand through the wind.
**Roots grow slowly** Roots deepen year after year. We grow in peace by learning of Him a little at a time.
Learn of me, and listen to my words; walk in the meekness of my Spirit, and you shall have peace in me.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
That peace comes from the assurances spoken by a still, small voice.
Grow slowly.
**Shade for others** A steady tree gives shade. Someone who has peace can offer it to others.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their faith kept them steady under pressure. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma's people in bondage

blocks.text: Alma and his people were under heavy burdens. They prayed, and the Lord answered.

And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders, that even you cannot feel them upon your backs, even while you are in bondage; and this will I do that ye may stand as witnesses for me hereafter, and that ye may know of a surety that I, the Lord God, do visit my people in their afflictions. And now it came to pass that the burdens which were laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light; yea, the Lord did strengthen them that they could bear up their burdens with ease, and they did submit cheerfully and with patience to all the will of the Lord.
The burdens weren't removed at once. They were made lighter. The Lord strengthened them, and peace came while they were still under load.

application.text: First, name one thing that feels heavy. Second, ask Heavenly Father to make it lighter, not just to take it away. Third, look for the strength that comes.

opening.text: A parent humming a lullaby in the middle of the night doesn't fix anything. The baby is still tired. The house is still dark. But the soft sound settles the child. Peace can come that way. A quiet voice, a steady presence, and the heart slows down. The Savior's peace is a lot like that.

mainMessage.text: Peace is a gentle voice that settles the heart, even when nothing around us has changed.

blocks.text: **Come close** A child comes close to hear the song. The Savior invites us the same way.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.
The Savior’s invitation to come to Him is an offer of peace.
Come close.
**A different kind of song** The world is loud and quick. The Savior is gentle.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.

**The voice in the dark** A lullaby is a voice, not a light. The Spirit speaks peace to us in the dark.
Did I not speak peace to your mind concerning the matter? What greater witness can you have than from God?
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “My Peace I Leave with You” from the April 2017 general conference.

These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
But we can have His peace with us irrespective of the troubles of the world.

**Learn the tune** A child learns a lullaby by hearing it often. We learn His peace the same way.
Learn of me, and listen to my words; walk in the meekness of my Spirit, and you shall have peace in me.
Elder Dennis E. Simmons of the Seventy said this in his talk “His Peace” from the April 1997 general conference.
That peace comes from the assurances spoken by a still, small voice.
Learn the tune.
**Sing it to someone else** What settled us can settle another. We can sing the song to those who can't sleep.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Finding Personal Peace” from the April 2023 general conference.

story.title: Peace in the prison

blocks.text: Nephi and Lehi were in a prison, surrounded by a crowd. A voice came to them.

And it came to pass that there came a voice unto them, yea, a pleasant voice, as if it were a whisper, saying: Peace, peace be unto you, because of your faith in my Well Beloved, who was from the foundation of the world.
The voice was pleasant, like a whisper. It came in a place of danger. Peace can reach us anywhere.
